findings.fix: drop policy "orders readable" on public.orders;  -- replace with e.g. using (user_id = (select auth.uid()))
findings.detail: USING (true) for anon: anyone with your anon key can read every row. Sensitive-looking columns: address.

findings.fix: alter table public.profiles enable row level security;  -- then add policies scoped to (select auth.uid())
findings.detail: Row Level Security is OFF. Anyone holding your public anon key (it ships in your frontend) can read every row and insert/update/delete rows through the REST API. Sensitive-looking columns: email, phone.

findings.fix: revoke all on public.user_emails from anon, authenticated;  -- or move it to a schema the API does not expose
findings.detail: This view reads from auth.users and is reachable through the API, exposing user accounts (columns: email).

findings.fix: Use app_metadata (only writable server-side) or a roles table checked with (select auth.uid()).
findings.detail: Policy reads user_metadata from the JWT. Users can set their own user_metadata with supabase.auth.updateUser(), so they can grant themselves this access (e.g. role = admin).

findings.fix: alter view public.order_summary set (security_invoker = true);
findings.detail: View runs with its owner's privileges (no security_invoker), so RLS on the tables underneath is ignored for whoever queries it.

findings.fix: revoke execute on function reset_order(integer) from public, anon, authenticated;  -- or add a check on (select auth.uid()) inside
findings.detail: Anyone with your anon key can call this via /rest/v1/rpc. It runs as its owner (skipping RLS), changes data, and has no visible check on who is calling. If it backs a public form (bookings, sign-ups), make sure it validates every input, only writes what a visitor should, and is rate-limited.

findings.fix: update storage.buckets set public = false where id = 'invoices';  -- then serve files with signed URLs
findings.detail: Public bucket: every file is downloadable by anyone with its URL, no login needed. Fine for avatars or marketing images, not for user documents.

findings.fix: drop policy "anyone uploads" on storage.objects;  -- restrict to: to authenticated with check (bucket_id = '...' and owner = (select auth.uid()))
findings.detail: Anyone with your anon key can upload files to your project. That invites abuse: malware hosting, phishing files and a growing storage bill.

findings.fix: revoke execute on function all_notes() from public, anon, authenticated;  -- or add a check on (select auth.uid()) inside
findings.detail: Any signed-in user can call this via /rest/v1/rpc. It runs as its owner (skipping RLS) and has no visible check on who is calling, so every user gets the same access.

findings.fix: alter function get_all_profiles() set search_path = '';  -- and schema-qualify names inside it
findings.detail: SECURITY DEFINER function without a fixed search_path can be tricked into running objects a caller controls.

findings.fix: revoke execute on function get_all_profiles() from public, anon, authenticated;  -- or add a check on (select auth.uid()) inside
findings.detail: Anyone with your anon key can call this via /rest/v1/rpc. It runs as its owner (skipping RLS) and has no visible check on who is calling. Fine only if everything it returns is meant to be public.

findings.fix: drop policy "anyone can submit" on public.feedback;  -- scope with: with check (user_id = (select auth.uid()))
findings.detail: Anyone with your anon key can insert rows. Fine for a public form if intended, but add validation and rate limiting.

findings.fix: drop policy "notes for users" on public.notes;  -- replace with e.g. using (user_id = (select auth.uid()))
findings.detail: USING (true) for authenticated: any signed-up user can read every row, and signup is usually open to anyone.

findings.fix: revoke select on public.order_stats from anon, authenticated;  -- serve it through a function or a private schema
findings.detail: Materialized views cannot have RLS. Everything in it is readable by anyone with your anon key.

findings.fix: revoke execute on function get_my_order(integer) from public, anon;  -- signed-in users keep access
findings.detail: Anonymous visitors can call this via /rest/v1/rpc. It does check the caller, so this is defense in depth: if it isn't meant to be public, revoking anon access removes the attack surface entirely.

findings.fix: drop policy "countries readable" on public.countries;  -- replace with e.g. using (user_id = (select auth.uid()))
findings.detail: USING (true) for authenticated on a table with no owner column: this looks like shared reference data that every signed-in user may read. Fine if so.

findings.fix: Wrap it: (select auth.uid()) instead of auth.uid().
findings.detail: auth.uid()/auth.jwt() is called once per row instead of once per query. Big slowdown on large tables.

findings.fix: -- if the app needs it: create policy "..." on public.audit_log for select to authenticated using (user_id = (select auth.uid()));
findings.detail: RLS is on with no policies, so the API can't read or write this table (only service_role can). Fine if intended; if your app uses it, it is silently getting empty results.
